text:
[IDAT.6.2.2] The `fired` flag implements refraction per
[LDET.5.3]: once an activation fires, it stays on
the agenda with `fired = true` until the LHS
changes, preventing re-fire on the same binding
tuple.

---

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_settled
idris.note: Marking a token fired keeps the table settled: `fired` is not part of what settledness looks at.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__pending_count_mark
idris.note: Marking a pending token lowers the pending count by exactly one.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__pending_mark_lte
idris.note: Marking never raises the pending count.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__pop_inv
idris.note: The pop (mark fired) preserves the invariant, leaves working memory alone, drops the firing stratum's pending count and no other's.

idris.name: Iret_11__tok
idris.note: A token carries `fired` and `blocked`; `fired` IS the refraction state, as the clause says, and stays set while the token is kept across re-propagation ([IRET.8.1]'s kept set).

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_at
idris.note: Set `fired` on the j-th token of a table.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_fired
idris.note: Set `fired` on entry j of rule r's table -- step 1e of [IRET.11.4], as a flag rather than a set insertion.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_t
idris.note: Set `fired` on one token.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__refresh_with
idris.note: The "until the LHS changes" half: a blocked -> unblocked transition is a re-propagation and clears `fired`; every other transition leaves it.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_act
idris.note: The fired flag: set on firing, kept until the LHS changes.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_acts
idris.note: Set `fired` on activation j of a terminal's list.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_chain
idris.note: Set `fired` on one activation of a chain.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_net
idris.note: Set `fired` on activation j of rule r.

idris.name: iret_11_3_1__first_unfired
idris.note: A fired activation stays on the agenda and is skipped.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_atuple
idris.note: Marking an activation fired leaves its tuple.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_chain_view
idris.note: Marking keeps a chain consistent.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_net_view
idris.note: SETTING `fired` keeps the view.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_tuples
idris.note: Marking an activation fired leaves the tuples.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__set_at_tuples
idris.note: Any change to one activation that leaves its tuple leaves the tuples.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_acts_count
idris.note: Marking an unfired activation lowers the terminal's unfired count by one.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_all
idris.note: Every activation of every chain marked fired; nothing else touched. What a run to quiescence leaves.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_all_acts
idris.note: Marking everything after marking one is marking everything.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_all_fired
idris.note: And so are chains with nothing unfired.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_all_set_at
idris.note: And over the chains.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_fired_acts
idris.note: A terminal with nothing unfired is unchanged by marking everything.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_net_count
idris.note: And over the chains: marking the selected activation lowers the count by one.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_twice
idris.note: Marking twice is marking once.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_live
idris.note: Setting `fired` leaves every activation live.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_sorted
idris.note: Setting `fired` on an activation keeps the terminal sorted: the flag is not a key.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_chain_ordered
idris.note: Marking keeps a chain's terminal in agenda order.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_net_ordered
idris.note: SETTING `fired` keeps the ordered view.

idris.name: Iret_11_3__refracted_fired
idris.note: The set is subsumed by the flag: every refracted identity's activation carries `fired`.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_fired
idris.note: A marked activation carries `fired`.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__marked_fired
idris.note: After marking activation j every activation with its identity carries `fired`: identities distinct, there is only the one.

idris.name: iret_11_3__refraction_after_history
idris.note: The clause's flag, kept until the LHS changes, is the whole of refraction in the tick-free fragment: the set of [IRET.11.3] never refuses beyond it.

idris.name: iret_11_4__mark_sound
idris.note: Setting `fired` keeps the ghost sound.

idris.name: ldet_5_8__tick_keeps_activation
idris.note: A TICK IS NOT A CHANGE TO THE LHS: an activation whose match the new test still admits is the same record after the tick, its `fired` flag included. A fired match stays refracted across every tick that leaves it matching -- Rete/NetworkRefraction.idr's theorem, restated under ticks.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__mark_agree_state
idris.note: Both sides mark the selected activation fired, and the agreement holds of the marked state.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__mark_agree
idris.note: MARKING THE SELECTED TOKEN marks the selected activation: the unblocked tokens after the mark are the terminal after its mark.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__mark_tables_agree
idris.note: Marking the selected token of the selected table marks the selected activation of the selected terminal; every other table and terminal stands.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__transfer
idris.note: THE TRANSFER THEOREM: run on one history from the loaded network and from FireLoop's empty state under the program the network lowers to, the two engines reach one working memory, and each table's unblocked tokens are its terminal's activations, in order and with their flags. Against the plain pipeline, inputs without Rete/PumpBoundary.idr's TMS phase and without the clock; Rete/NetworkTmsTransfer.idr carries the phase and Rete/NetworkTtl.idr the clock, on this agreement.

idris.name: Rlow_4_2_1__tables_agree
idris.note: Each table's unblocked tokens are the corresponding terminal's activations, in order and with their `fired` flags.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__prop_agree
idris.note: THE UNBLOCKED TOKENS AFTER A PROPAGATION ARE THE NETWORK'S ACTIVATIONS after the same change: the tuples agree because both sides hold exactly the unblocked matches in the key's order and two sorted lists with the same members are one list; the flags agree because an activation whose match survives is kept on both sides, and a released or new match is unfired on both.

idris.name: Iret_8_1__evolves
idris.note: What refraction needs of a terminal's evolution: an old activation whose match survives keeps its flag.

idris.name: iret_19_1__insert_flags
idris.note: INSERTING A FRESH FACT: every activation afterwards is an old one or unfired, and every old activation whose match survives is still there, flag and all -- an assertion creates only matches holding the new fact, so no old match is created anew.

idris.name: iret_19_2__retract_flags
idris.note: RETRACTING A LIVE FACT: every activation afterwards is an old one or unfired, and every old activation whose match survives is still there, flag and all -- a retraction ends only matches holding the fact, and no surviving match holds it.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_tables_well
idris.note: Marking one token of one table keeps every table well-formed.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_well
idris.note: Marking a token fired keeps a table well-formed: the flag moves no tuple.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_keeps_live
idris.note: Marking a token fired ends no activation.
